commit.message:
fix(labs): align chat-control-plane behavior labs with the R-series runtime contracts

Layered staleness exposed after the contract pin repair (PR #65 first
commit): each unblocked CI step revealed the next pre-existing stale
expectation at the compute-browser stack heads.

1. tests/chat_bridge_worker_combined_load_behavior.mjs
   - A2_OPERATOR_RUNTIME hand pin '0.6.2-auto-rollover' -> derived from
     runtime-package-manifest.json operator_runtime (drift-immune).
   - The lab seeded armed=false yet expected an immediate /v1/commands/next
     fetch — stale v0.6.2 behavior. The R-series runtime deliberately
     suppresses the command fetch while disarmed (v0.6.3 DISARM fetch
     suppression, closes the live command regeneration storm). The lab now
     asserts BOTH sides of the invariant: disarmed load issues zero remote
     calls and persists bridgeCommandFetchSuppressed='DISARMED'; arming via
     the storage-change path unlocks the poll and sources the pairing
     header from the IndexedDB vault. Strictly stronger than the original
     one-sided expectation.

2. tests/adversarial_chat_bridge_dom_f7.mjs
   - manifest version hand pin '0.6.2' -> derived from
     runtime-package-manifest.json package_version.
   - content_scripts entry pin updated from the retired versioned filename
     content-recovery-v062.js to the packaged content-recovery.js (policy:
     reject_versioned_runtime_files); the recovery source read now targets
     the packaged file instead of the byte-identical legacy orphan.

Local full-battery verification at parent 7555c2c (c50dd086 lineage):
44/44 pytest (bridge contract 15 + receipt 12 + remote 9 + debugger
integration 8) and 6/6 node labs green.

(mailbox #224/#229); tests-only change, no production code touched.
